subject: English
passage: Democracy and Education is a 1916 nonfiction work by John Dewey. In the text, the author emphasizes the importance of developing individual abilities rather than standardizing students: ______
prompt: Which quotation from Democracy and Education most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "If the school is to be a preparation for social life—why not organize it on the same plan as society itself?"
choices.B: "Our educational value is seen to lie not so much in what we are as separate beings, as in our capacity to work together toward common ends."
choices.C: "We do not foolishly measure the oak by the pine, and praise the pine for surpassing the oak—nor urge the oak to [imitate] the pine. We tend both, each to its fullest expression—and are the richer."
choices.D: "That every child shall have conditions favorable to the fullest growth; that every student, from youth to maturity, shall have opportunity to learn all they are capable of [mastering], to develop every capacity within them."

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it effectively illustrates both components of the claim. The oak and pine metaphor explicitly rejects standardization and comparison: 'We do not foolishly measure the oak by the pine, and praise the pine for surpassing the oak—nor urge the oak to [imitate] the pine.' This directly addresses avoiding standardized measures. The quotation then advocates for individual development: 'We tend both, each to its fullest expression.' This parallel structure captures Dewey's philosophy of nurturing unique individual capacities rather than imposing uniform standards.
